 Warm Weekend in the 80s, Rain Returns for Halloween | October 22, 2026 
 Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 4:23 PM CDT | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google Friday will be a sunny to mostly sunny day with highs in the low to middle 80s. Light winds and mostly clear skies are expected for high school football Friday night, with temperatures dropping into the 60s. This weekend will feature highs in the 80s under a range of mostly sunny to mostly cloudy skies. A low chance for rain remains in the forecast for Tuesday, then higher chances for rain are in the forecast for the end of next week. We are continuing to give the first alert to the possibility of rain on Halloween.
Today in weather history... October 22, 2017, a single megaflash lightning bolt was captured by NOAA’s GOES-16 satellite. The horizontal distance of the bolt stretched 515 miles from eastern TX to near Kansas City, MO. In July 2025, the WMO certified the measurement as a world record. Today's daily weather history segment comes to us courtesy of the Southeast Regional Climate Center.
Also on today's edition of First Alert Weather Extra... we're taking a look at flooding in the west and southwest U.S. from recent thunderstorms, as well as some of the ecological impacts of the war in Iran. In closing, our satellite imagery of the day, showing the powerful low along the East Coast evolved into Subtropical Storm Josephine, courtesy of the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere.  Your First Alert: Halloween Rain Could Impact Trick-or-Treating | October 21, 2026 
 Updated : Oct. 21, 2026 at 4:48 PM CDT Temperatures through the end of the week will run near to slightly above normal for late October, lows in the 50s and highs in the 70s/low 80s. The forecast remains dry until Tuesday of next week, when a front will bring a low chance for rain to East Texas. The next best chance for rain will not be until next weekend, Halloween weekend. This is your first alert that trick-or-treating the night of Halloween could be affected by showers and thunderstorms. 
Today in weather history... October 21, 1934, a severe windstorm lashed the northern Pacific coast. The system claimed 22 lives in Washington State and caused ~$1.7 million in damage. Winds gusting to 87 mph at North Head, WA, produced waves twenty feet high on the Puget Sound. Today's daily weather history segment comes to us courtesy of the Southeast Regional Climate Center.
This week's weather word is "ora." (Also spelled aura.) A regular valley wind at Lake Garda in Italy. This definition comes from the American Meteorological Society's Glossary of Meteorology (2026).
Also on today's edition of First Alert Weather Extra... a SpaceX launch this week created another “jellyfish” cloud this week, and the winner of the Small World Micrography competition has been named. In closing, our satellite imagery of the day, showing Anak Krakatau, where the legendary Krakatoa once resided, experiencing a volcanic eruption several weeks ago, courtesy of the Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere.
